meta: A whaling ship and a schooner off the cliffs of Gay Head in William Bradford's Whaler off the Vineyard, about 1850.
about: William Bradford is best known for Arctic paintings, but his early work focused on the ships of New England. He grew up near New Bedford, Massachusetts, home to a successful whaling industry. Here a large whaling ship sails behind a smaller schooner in the foreground, with the cliffs of Gay Head on Martha's Vineyard behind. This was the standard route for whalers entering and leaving New Bedford. Bradford stressed the smallest details, from ripples in the sails to the suspenders on the sailors.

meta: The old king Solomon kneels in a temple beside one of his wives in Salomon Koninck's Idolatry of King Solomon, 1644.
about: In the middle the old king kneels in the temple beside one of his wives. At the left are the altar and a priest with a censer, with a servant and a sacrificial animal in the foreground. At the right is the king's retinue, with a servant carrying a parasol. Salomon Koninck signed and dated the painting 1644.

meta: Jephthah's daughter greets her father with a tambourine at a city gate in Jacob Savery's landscape of about 1580.
about: A mountain landscape has a city in a valley. At the left is the city gate, where the daughter of Jephthah plays a tambourine to greet her father. Far behind stretches a wide landscape with a large church and more buildings at the edge of a bay. Jacob Savery painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1580.

meta: Orpheus leads Eurydice out of Hades while Pluto and Proserpine watch, in Jean Raoux's painting of about 1709.
about: In the center, Orpheus leads his wife Eurydice out of Hades after winning her release with his enchanting violin playing. Pluto, ruler of Hades, and his wife Proserpine watch them leave from the upper left. The three Fates spin the future at the left, ominously foreshadowing what will happen to Orpheus. Jean Raoux painted it around 1709, and it is in the Getty.

meta: Naked girls swim and sit on seaside rocks while a ship passes in John Macallan Swan's The Sirens, 1870.
about: Naked girls swim and sit on the rocks on the shore of a sea. A ship with white sails is far off, and gulls fly in the air. John Macallan Swan painted The Sirens, and the catalog dates it to 1870.

meta: Ships at sea near a coast in a storm in the Strait of Dover, painted by Louis Meijer in 1819.
about: This is a storm in the Strait of Dover, with ships at sea near a coast. Louis Meijer painted it in 1819, and the Rijksmuseum holds it. The museum's note describes nothing beyond the ships and the storm.

meta: A man in armor in an oval within a panel with a trophy of arms, a design by Francesco de Mura, about 1740.
about: A half-length portrait of a man in armor is sketched in an oval frame. The surrounding vertical panel is decorated with a trophy of arms, two putti, masks at the top and bottom, and an escutcheon with a crown above it. Francesco de Mura made the design around 1740.

meta: Francesco Pesellino's King Melchior Sailing to the Holy Land, about 1445 to 1450, a pendant to a Magi procession by Zanobi Strozzi.
about: King Melchior Sailing to the Holy Land is a panel of about 1445 to 1450 in tempera, oil and gold by Pesellino. Sterling and Francine Clark acquired it before 1955, and it is now in the Clark Art Institute. It is now known to be a pair with The Procession of the Magi by Zanobi Strozzi. With another, unidentified painting, they may have formed the predella of an altarpiece that has not been identified.

meta: Designs for two ewers and a bowl with a swing handle, among them a ewer shaped like an armless woman, by Luzio Romano, about 1540.
about: At the left is a design for a bowl with a swing handle. The handle, with applied female forms, is made of double arches joined in the middle by a ring and hooked to the bowl's rim between the horns of goats' heads. The body has draped festoons, acanthus leaves and a female mask with a fan diadem. Below at the center is a small ewer shaped as an armless, elongated woman, whose head supports a shell spout. Luzio Romano made the sheet.

meta: An open-air theater show draws a crowd, with a pancake seller and children in a goat cart, in Matthijs Naiveu's painting of about 1670.
about: A theatrical performance takes place in the open air. At the right a man and a woman lie in the grass by a thistle, and she points to the show. A crowd has gathered in front of the stage, with a pancake seller at the left, children in a goat cart in the middle and an officer on horseback at the right. On the stage a dancing couple and a harlequin playing the violin perform, and the stage is hung with the arms of the provinces. Matthijs Naiveu painted it.

meta: George Washington, painted by Robert Edge Pine during a three-week stay at Mount Vernon in 1785.
about: George Washington did not always enjoy sitting for portraits, but the British-born Robert Edge Pine came highly recommended. Francis Hopkinson wrote that Pine's zeal for the American cause had brought him from England to secure real portraits, not ideal pictures. In the spring of 1785 Pine spent three weeks with Washington and his family at Mount Vernon. Afterward Washington wrote that he was so used to painters that he sat like patience on a monument.

meta: A triptych on art training, with a nursery as nature, a night school and a scholar cutting a pen, by Willem Joseph Laquy, about 1770.
about: This triptych is an allegory of art education. The middle panel shows a lying-in room, where a woman nurses a child at a table, with a cradle and a basket on the floor, a chandelier above and a stuffed deer's head on the wall. A dentist is in the background. The room stands for nature. The left panel shows an evening school where writing is learned by candlelight, standing for education, and on the right a scholar cuts a pen in his study. Willem Joseph Laquy painted it.

meta: Edwin Landseer posed as the young Earl of Rutland in Charles Robert Leslie's Murder of Rutland by Lord Clifford, 1815.
about: The Murder of Rutland by Lord Clifford is a history painting of 1815 by Charles Robert Leslie. It shows a scene from the Wars of the Roses, inspired by Shakespeare's Henry VI, Part 3, in which the young Edmund, Earl of Rutland, is killed by Lord Clifford after the Battle of Wakefield in 1460. Leslie had his friend Edwin Landseer, then a student at the Royal Academy Schools, model Rutland, and Landseer later remembered it fondly. It is at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts in Philadelphia.

meta: The Incredulity of Saint Thomas in tempera by Emmanuel Tzanes, a prolific painter of the 1600s.
about: The Incredulity of Saint Thomas is a tempera painting by the Greek painter Emmanuel Tzanes. His catalog runs to over a hundred works, and he was one of the most prolific painters of the 1600s, working in Crete and also Corfu and Venice. His two brothers, Marinos and Konstantinos Tzanes, were also well-known painters, and Marinos wrote the poem The Cretan War. All three belonged to the Late Cretan School and the early Heptanese School.
